Full-Time & Part-Time Bus Drivers Wanted

Whether you are a seasoned pro looking for a better work-life balance or a motivated individual ready to jumpstart a new career, we have a seat for you. Enjoy the beauty of our Montana roads while making a real impact in your community.

Position Overview

The Temporary Student & Family Support Liaison provides short-term direct operational support to the High School Counseling Department during a period of staff FMLA leave. This role serves as a primary communication hub and triage specialist, handling routine parent inquiries, non-emergency student walk-ins, and teacher coordination. By managing front-line communication and daily operational traffic, this role allows permanent, credentialed school counselors to focus on master scheduling, credit/graduation audits, and specialized crisis care.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Front-Line Triage & Walk-Ins: Manage non-emergency student walk-ins, provide initial supportive listening, and triage urgent mental health or safety concerns immediately to permanent, credentialed counseling staff.
  • Parent & Family Communication: Serve as the primary point of contact for incoming parent phone calls and emails regarding general student well-being, routine classroom concerns, and navigation of school resources.
  • Teacher & Staff Liaison: Field day-to-day teacher inquiries regarding student progress, classroom accommodations, and routine behavioral/academic check-ins.
  • Communication & Inbox Management: Monitor and help filter department inbox inquiries, resolving routine support requests directly while routing complex academic, scheduling, or confidential matters to assigned counselors.
  • Resource Coordination: Assist families and students by connecting them with established internal district support programs and external community services as needed.
  • Professional Standards: Maintain strict student privacy under FERPA and adhere to trauma-informed, professional communication standards with all students, including neurodivergent populations.

Note: Direct clinical crisis management, formal IEP/504 case management, and official graduation credit audits remain exclusively with permanent, credentialed counseling staff.

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Human Services, Psychology, Education, or a closely related field required.
  • Experience: Minimum of 1–2 years of experience working with adolescents in a school, human services, youth program, or mental health setting preferred.
  • Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills; demonstrated ability to de-escalate emotional situations with students and parents; strong organizational and computer literacy skills.
  • Knowledge & Abilities: Demonstrated understanding of student confidentiality laws (FERPA), professional boundaries, and inclusive practices for diverse and neurodivergent student populations. State counseling endorsement is not required for this support liaison role.

This is a temporary, short-term assignment created strictly to provide coverage during an approved employee leave of absence. Employment will terminate automatically upon the return of the regular employee from leave
